---
title: "Class 12: The Spatial Mapping"
subtitle: "From the parent domain to a physical element"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
---

[Class 11](11_Class.qmd) showed how to build 2D basis functions on the **parent domain** (also called the **reference domain**), the square $\hat\Omega = [-1,1]^2$ with coordinates $(\xi,\eta)$. 
Elements in a mesh may not be squares, and if they are, they aren't always centered around the origin, so we need a method that takes a point of the parent domain to a point of the element. 
That rule is the **spatial mapping**, and it uses the same basis functions. 
In two dimensions, this looks like

$$
\underline{x}^e(\xi,\eta) = \sum_{A=0}^{n_{en}-1} \underline{x}_A^e \, N_A(\xi,\eta),
$$

where $\underline{x}_A^e$ is the position of node $A$ of element $e$, and
$n_{en} = (p_\xi+1)(p_\eta+1)$ is the number of nodes on the element. 
The above equation can be represented by two coordinate mappings for both the $x$ and the $y$ coordinates from the parent domain as

$$
x(\xi,\eta) = \sum_A x_A\,N_A(\xi,\eta), \qquad
y(\xi,\eta) = \sum_A y_A\,N_A(\xi,\eta).
$$

Compare this with the approximate solution,

$$
u^h(\xi,\eta) = \sum_A d_A\,N_A(\xi,\eta).
$$

Both of these maps use the same basis functions but different coefficients, which coefficients are defined by the nodal positions of the element geometry.
Using the same $N_A$ for both the solution, $u^h,$ and for the geometry is what **isoparametric** means.

## The general form

If we write $\underline{\xi}$ for the parametric coordinates, $\underline{\xi} = (\xi,\eta)$ in 2D and $\underline{\xi} = (\xi,\eta,\zeta)$ in 3D. Then

$$
\underline{x}^e(\underline{\xi}) = \sum_{A=0}^{n_{en}-1} \underline{x}_A^e \, N_A(\underline{\xi}),
$$

with the basis functions and the single index built as in Class 11,

$$
N_A(\underline{\xi}) = \prod_{i=0}^{n_{sd}-1} \ell^{p_i}_{a_i}(\xi_i),
\qquad
A = \sum_{i=0}^{n_{sd}-1} a_i\,s_i,
\qquad
s_0 = 1, \quad s_i = \prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(p_j+1),
$$

and $n_{en} = \prod_{i=0}^{n_{sd}-1}(p_i+1)$. 
In 2D this is $N_A(\xi,\eta) = \ell^{p_\xi}_a(\xi)\,\ell^{p_\eta}_b(\eta)$ with $A = a + (p_\xi+1)b$, which is what the viewer below uses. 
The interpolation points are typicallly equally spaced in each direction.

## The map, interactively

The left panel is the parent domain, the right is the physical element. The element you
start with is a quarter annulus, $1 \le r \le 2$, with its nodes placed at the parametric
node locations.

* Drag the dot in the parent domain, or type $\xi$ and $\eta$ below it. The matching
  point in the physical element follows.
* Drag the gold control points in the physical element, or edit their coordinates in the
  table. The element changes shape.
* Nodes in the parent domain are drawn scaled by $N_A(\xi,\eta)$ at the current point, so
  a large marker means a large weight. Blue is a positive weight, red a negative one.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-controls">

    <div class="sm-row"><label for="pxi">p<sub>ξ</sub> (degree)</label><input id="pxi" type="range" min="1" max="3" step="1" value="2"><output id="pxi_o"></output></div>
    <div class="sm-row"><label for="peta">p<sub>η</sub> (degree)</label><input id="peta" type="range" min="1" max="3" step="1" value="2"><output id="peta_o"></output></div>
  </div>
  <div>
    <div class="sm-row"><label for="xi">ξ</label><input id="xi" type="range" min="-1" max="1" step="0.005" value="0.35"><input id="xi_n" type="number" min="-1" max="1" step="0.01" value="0.35"></div>
    <div class="sm-row"><label for="eta">η</label><input id="eta" type="range" min="-1" max="1" step="0.005" value="-0.25"><input id="eta_n" type="number" min="-1" max="1" step="0.01" value="-0.25"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="sm-toggles">

    <button class="sm-btn" id="b_reset">reset element</button>
    <button class="sm-btn" id="b_fit">fit view</button>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="sm-pair">
  <div class="sm-panel">
    <h4>Parent domain &nbsp;<span style="font-weight:400;color:#6b7684">(ξ, η) ∈ [−1,1]²</span></h4>
    <svg id="svg_par" class="sm-svg" viewBox="0 0 440 440"></svg>
  </div>
  <div class="sm-panel">
    <h4>Physical domain &nbsp;<span style="font-weight:400;color:#6b7684">(x, y)</span></h4>
    <svg id="svg_phy" class="sm-svg" viewBox="0 0 440 440"></svg>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="sm-grid">
  <div>
    <div class="sm-tablewrap">
      <table class="sm-cp">
        <thead><tr><th>A</th><th>(a, b)</th><th>x<sub>A</sub></th><th>y<sub>A</sub></th><th>N<sub>A</sub>(ξ,η)</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody id="cp_rows"></tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
    <div class="sm-note" id="sum_note"></div>
  </div>
  <div>
    <div class="sm-chain">
      <span class="lbl">1 — the sum, symbolically</span>
      <span class="eq" id="eq1"></span>
      <span class="lbl">2 — nodal coordinates substituted</span>
      <span class="eq" id="eq2"></span>
      <span class="lbl">3 — basis functions evaluated at (ξ, η)</span>
      <span class="eq" id="eq3"></span>
      <span class="lbl">4 — the mapped point</span>
      <span class="eq res" id="eq4"></span>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const VB = 440, PAD = 34;
const C = {xi:"#1f5fbf", eta:"#c2410c", node:"#e0a800", ink:"#18202b",
           grey:"#9aa3ae", neg:"#2f6db5", pos:"#b8322a", faint:"#dfe4ea"};

/* ---------- 1D Lagrange machinery (equally spaced points) ---------- */
const nodes1d = p => Array.from({length:p+1}, (_,i) => -1 + 2*i/p);

function lag(p, a, t){
  const P = nodes1d(p);
  let v = 1;
  for (let j = 0; j <= p; j++) if (j !== a) v *= (t - P[j])/(P[a] - P[j]);
  return v;
}

/* ---------- state ---------- */
const st = {pxi:2, peta:2, xi:0.35, eta:-0.25, cp:[], view:null, drag:null};

// default element: a quarter annulus, 1 <= r <= 2, 0 <= theta <= pi/2,
// sampled at the parametric node locations. Curved, and detJ > 0 at every degree.
function defaultCP(pxi, peta){
  const r0=1, r1=2, t0=0, t1=Math.PI/2, out=[];
  const Pa = nodes1d(pxi), Pb = nodes1d(peta);
  for (let b = 0; b <= peta; b++){
    const th = t0 + (t1-t0)*(Pb[b]+1)/2;
    for (let a = 0; a <= pxi; a++){
      const r = r0 + (r1-r0)*(Pa[a]+1)/2;
      out.push([r*Math.cos(th), r*Math.sin(th)]);
    }
  }
  return out;
}

const nen  = () => (st.pxi+1)*(st.peta+1);
const idxA = (a,b) => a + (st.pxi+1)*b;
const ab   = A => [A % (st.pxi+1), Math.floor(A/(st.pxi+1))];

// weights N_A at a parametric point
function weights(xi, eta){
  const w = new Array(nen());
  for (let b = 0; b <= st.peta; b++){
    const lb = lag(st.peta, b, eta);
    for (let a = 0; a <= st.pxi; a++) w[idxA(a,b)] = lag(st.pxi, a, xi) * lb;
  }
  return w;
}

function mapPt(xi, eta){
  const w = weights(xi, eta);
  let x = 0, y = 0;
  for (let A = 0; A < w.length; A++){ x += st.cp[A][0]*w[A]; y += st.cp[A][1]*w[A]; }
  return [x, y];
}

/* ---------- coordinate transforms for a panel ---------- */
// equal aspect, data range -> viewBox pixels
function makeTx(x0, x1, y0, y1){
  const iw = VB - 2*PAD, ih = VB - 2*PAD;
  const s = Math.min(iw/Math.max(x1-x0, 1e-9), ih/Math.max(y1-y0, 1e-9));
  const cx = (x0+x1)/2, cy = (y0+y1)/2;
  return {
    s,
    px: x => VB/2 + (x - cx)*s,
    py: y => VB/2 - (y - cy)*s,       // flip: +y is up
    dx: px => cx + (px - VB/2)/s,
    dy: py => cy - (py - VB/2)/s
  };
}
const parTx = () => makeTx(-1.18, 1.18, -1.18, 1.18);

function fitView(){
  let x0=1e9,x1=-1e9,y0=1e9,y1=-1e9;
  const bump = (x,y)=>{x0=Math.min(x0,x);x1=Math.max(x1,x);y0=Math.min(y0,y);y1=Math.max(y1,y);};
  for (const [x,y] of st.cp) bump(x,y);
  const M = 25;                                  // sample the mapped boundary too
  for (let i = 0; i <= M; i++){
    const t = -1 + 2*i/M;
    for (const q of [[t,-1],[t,1],[-1,t],[1,t]]){ const p = mapPt(q[0],q[1]); bump(p[0],p[1]); }
  }
  const mx = 0.12*Math.max(x1-x0, y1-y0, 1e-6);
  st.view = [x0-mx, x1+mx, y0-mx, y1+mx];
}
const phyTx = () => makeTx(st.view[0], st.view[1], st.view[2], st.view[3]);

/* ---------- small svg helpers ---------- */
const esc = s => String(s);
const line = (x1,y1,x2,y2,st_) => `<line x1="${x1.toFixed(2)}" y1="${y1.toFixed(2)}" x2="${x2.toFixed(2)}" y2="${y2.toFixed(2)}" ${st_}/>`;
const poly = (pxy,st_) => `<polyline points="${pxy.map(p=>p[0].toFixed(2)+','+p[1].toFixed(2)).join(' ')}" fill="none" ${st_}/>`;
const circ = (x,y,r,st_) => `<circle cx="${x.toFixed(2)}" cy="${y.toFixed(2)}" r="${r.toFixed(2)}" ${st_}/>`;
const text = (x,y,s,st_) => `<text x="${x.toFixed(2)}" y="${y.toFixed(2)}" ${st_}>${esc(s)}</text>`;

const NSAMP = 41;
const samples = n => Array.from({length:n}, (_,i) => -1 + 2*i/(n-1));

/* ---------- parent panel ---------- */
function drawParent(w){
  const T = parTx(), o = [];
  const gl = 'stroke="'+C.faint+'" stroke-width="1"';

  // light grid at the interpolation lines
  for (const v of nodes1d(st.pxi)) o.push(line(T.px(v),T.py(-1),T.px(v),T.py(1), gl));
  for (const v of nodes1d(st.peta)) o.push(line(T.px(-1),T.py(v),T.px(1),T.py(v), gl));

  // the square
  o.push(`<rect x="${T.px(-1).toFixed(2)}" y="${T.py(1).toFixed(2)}" width="${(2*T.s).toFixed(2)}" height="${(2*T.s).toFixed(2)}" fill="none" stroke="${C.ink}" stroke-width="2"/>`);

  // crosshair at the current point
  o.push(line(T.px(st.xi),T.py(-1),T.px(st.xi),T.py(1), `stroke="${C.xi}" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-dasharray="4 3"`));
  o.push(line(T.px(-1),T.py(st.eta),T.px(1),T.py(st.eta), `stroke="${C.eta}" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-dasharray="4 3"`));

  // nodes, scaled by weight
  const scaleOn = $("t_weights").checked, labOn = $("t_labels").checked;
  for (let A = 0; A < nen(); A++){
    const [a,b] = ab(A);
    const X = T.px(nodes1d(st.pxi)[a]), Y = T.py(nodes1d(st.peta)[b]);
    const wv = w[A], r = scaleOn ? 3.5 + 13*Math.min(Math.abs(wv),1.35) : 6;
    const fill = Math.abs(wv) < 1e-12 ? C.grey : (wv > 0 ? C.neg : C.pos);
    o.push(circ(X, Y, r, `fill="${fill}" fill-opacity="${scaleOn?0.75:0.9}" stroke="${C.ink}" stroke-width="1"`));
    if (labOn) o.push(text(X, Y - r - 5, A, `text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="${C.ink}" font-family="monospace"`));
  }

  // the evaluation point
  o.push(circ(T.px(st.xi), T.py(st.eta), 7, `fill="#fff" stroke="${C.ink}" stroke-width="2.4"`));
  o.push(circ(T.px(st.xi), T.py(st.eta), 2.6, `fill="${C.ink}"`));

  // axis ticks
  o.push(text(T.px(0), T.py(-1)+20, "ξ", `text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="${C.xi}" font-style="italic"`));
  o.push(text(T.px(-1)-16, T.py(0)+4, "η", `text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="${C.eta}" font-style="italic"`));
  o.push(text(T.px(st.xi), T.py(1)-8, `(${st.xi.toFixed(3)}, ${st.eta.toFixed(3)})`,
        `text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-family="monospace" fill="${C.ink}"`));

  $("svg_par").innerHTML = o.join("");
}

/* ---------- physical panel ---------- */
function drawPhysical(w){
  const T = phyTx(), o = [];
  const S = samples(NSAMP);

  // mapped grid lines: images of constant eta (blue) and constant xi (orange)
  if ($("t_grid").checked){
    const NL = 7;
    for (let k = 0; k < NL; k++){
      const c = -1 + 2*k/(NL-1);
      o.push(poly(S.map(t => { const p = mapPt(t, c); return [T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1])]; }),
             `stroke="${C.xi}" stroke-width="0.9" stroke-opacity="0.55"`));
      o.push(poly(S.map(t => { const p = mapPt(c, t); return [T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1])]; }),
             `stroke="${C.eta}" stroke-width="0.9" stroke-opacity="0.55"`));
    }
  }

  // element boundary
  for (const e of [[-1,'eta'],[1,'eta'],[-1,'xi'],[1,'xi']]){
    const pts_ = S.map(t => { const p = e[1]==='eta' ? mapPt(t, e[0]) : mapPt(e[0], t); return [T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1])]; });
    o.push(poly(pts_, `stroke="${C.ink}" stroke-width="2.2"`));
  }

  // images of the current xi and eta lines
  o.push(poly(S.map(t => { const p = mapPt(st.xi, t); return [T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1])]; }),
         `stroke="${C.xi}" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="4 3"`));
  o.push(poly(S.map(t => { const p = mapPt(t, st.eta); return [T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1])]; }),
         `stroke="${C.eta}" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-dasharray="4 3"`));

  // control points
  const labOn = $("t_labels").checked;
  for (let A = 0; A < nen(); A++){
    const X = T.px(st.cp[A][0]), Y = T.py(st.cp[A][1]);
    const hot = st.drag && st.drag.kind === 'cp' && st.drag.A === A;
    o.push(circ(X, Y, hot ? 8.5 : 6.5, `fill="${C.node}" stroke="${C.ink}" stroke-width="1.6" style="cursor:grab"`));
    if (labOn) o.push(text(X + 10, Y - 8, A, `font-size="11" fill="${C.ink}" font-family="monospace"`));
  }

  // mapped evaluation point
  const p = mapPt(st.xi, st.eta);
  o.push(circ(T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1]), 7, `fill="#fff" stroke="${C.ink}" stroke-width="2.4"`));
  o.push(circ(T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1]), 2.6, `fill="${C.ink}"`));
  o.push(text(T.px(p[0]), T.py(p[1]) - 13, `(${p[0].toFixed(3)}, ${p[1].toFixed(3)})`,
        `text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-family="monospace" fill="${C.ink}"`));

  $("svg_phy").innerHTML = o.join("");
}

/* ---------- the symbolic chain ---------- */
const SUB = "₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉";
const sub = n => String(n).split("").map(d => SUB[+d]).join("");
const f3 = v => (Math.abs(v) < 5e-4 ? 0 : v).toFixed(3);
const f4 = v => (Math.abs(v) < 5e-5 ? 0 : v).toFixed(4);

function drawChain(w){
  const n = nen();
  let big = 0;
  for (let A = 1; A < n; A++) if (Math.abs(w[A]) > Math.abs(w[big])) big = A;

  const t1 = [], t2 = [], t3 = [];
  for (let A = 0; A < n; A++){
    const mark = A === big ? ' class="big"' : '';
    t1.push(`<span${mark}>x${sub(A)}·N${sub(A)}(ξ,η)</span>`);
    t2.push(`<span${mark}>(${f3(st.cp[A][0])}, ${f3(st.cp[A][1])})·N${sub(A)}(ξ,η)</span>`);
    t3.push(`<span${mark}>(${f3(st.cp[A][0])}, ${f3(st.cp[A][1])})·(${f4(w[A])})</span>`);
  }
  const p = mapPt(st.xi, st.eta);

  $("eq1").innerHTML = "x(ξ,η) = " + t1.join("  +  ");
  $("eq2").innerHTML = "       = " + t2.join("  +  ");
  $("eq3").innerHTML = "       = " + t3.join("  +  ");
  $("eq4").innerHTML = `       = (${p[0].toFixed(4)}, ${p[1].toFixed(4)})`;

  const s = w.reduce((q,v) => q+v, 0);
  const bad = Math.abs(s - 1) > 1e-9;
  $("sum_note").innerHTML =
    `Σ<sub>A</sub> N<sub>A</sub>(ξ,η) = <b>${s.toFixed(10)}</b> ` +
    (bad ? '<span class="sm-warn">— that should be 1</span>'
         : '— the partition of unity, at every point, for every degree.');
}

/* ---------- table ---------- */
function drawTable(w){
  const rows = [];
  let big = 0;
  for (let A = 1; A < nen(); A++) if (Math.abs(w[A]) > Math.abs(w[big])) big = A;
  for (let A = 0; A < nen(); A++){
    const [a,b] = ab(A);
    rows.push(
      `<tr class="${A===big?'hot':''}"><td>${A}</td><td>(${a}, ${b})</td>` +
      `<td><input type="number" step="0.05" data-A="${A}" data-c="0" value="${st.cp[A][0].toFixed(4)}"></td>` +
      `<td><input type="number" step="0.05" data-A="${A}" data-c="1" value="${st.cp[A][1].toFixed(4)}"></td>` +
      `<td>${f4(w[A])}</td></tr>`);
  }
  $("cp_rows").innerHTML = rows.join("");
  for (const inp of $("cp_rows").querySelectorAll("input")){
    inp.addEventListener("change", e => {
      const A = +e.target.getAttribute("data-A");
      const c = +e.target.getAttribute("data-c");
      const v = parseFloat(e.target.value);
      if (Number.isFinite(v)){ st.cp[A][c] = v; render(false); }
    });
  }
}

/* ---------- render ---------- */
let w = [];
function render(retable = true){
  $("pxi_o").value = st.pxi; $("peta_o").value = st.peta;
  $("xi").value = st.xi;  $("xi_n").value  = st.xi.toFixed(3);
  $("eta").value = st.eta; $("eta_n").value = st.eta.toFixed(3);
  w = weights(st.xi, st.eta);
  if (!st.view) fitView();
  drawParent(w);
  drawPhysical(w);
  drawChain(w);
  if (retable) drawTable(w);
  else { // just refresh the weight column without rebuilding the inputs
    const tds = $("cp_rows").querySelectorAll("tr");
    let big = 0;
    for (let A = 1; A < nen(); A++) if (Math.abs(w[A]) > Math.abs(w[big])) big = A;
    tds.forEach((tr, A) => {
      tr.className = A === big ? 'hot' : '';
      tr.lastElementChild.textContent = f4(w[A]);
    });
  }
}

/* ---------- pointer interaction ---------- */
function svgPt(svg, ev){
  const r = svg.getBoundingClientRect();
  return [(ev.clientX - r.left)*(VB/r.width), (ev.clientY - r.top)*(VB/r.height)];
}
const clamp = v => Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, v));

$("svg_par").addEventListener("pointerdown", ev => {
  const T = parTx(), [px,py] = svgPt($("svg_par"), ev);
  st.xi = clamp(T.dx(px)); st.eta = clamp(T.dy(py));
  st.drag = {kind:'pt'};
  $("svg_par").setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId);
  render(false);
});
$("svg_par").addEventListener("pointermove", ev => {
  if (!st.drag || st.drag.kind !== 'pt') return;
  const T = parTx(), [px,py] = svgPt($("svg_par"), ev);
  st.xi = clamp(T.dx(px)); st.eta = clamp(T.dy(py));
  render(false);
});

$("svg_phy").addEventListener("pointerdown", ev => {
  const T = phyTx(), [px,py] = svgPt($("svg_phy"), ev);
  let best = -1, bd = 14;                       // grab radius in viewBox units
  for (let A = 0; A < nen(); A++){
    const d = Math.hypot(px - T.px(st.cp[A][0]), py - T.py(st.cp[A][1]));
    if (d < bd){ bd = d; best = A; }
  }
  if (best < 0) return;
  st.drag = {kind:'cp', A:best};
  $("svg_phy").setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId);
  render(false);
});
$("svg_phy").addEventListener("pointermove", ev => {
  if (!st.drag || st.drag.kind !== 'cp') return;
  const T = phyTx(), [px,py] = svgPt($("svg_phy"), ev);
  st.cp[st.drag.A] = [T.dx(px), T.dy(py)];
  render(true);
});

for (const sv of ["svg_par","svg_phy"]){
  $(sv).addEventListener("pointerup",  () => { st.drag = null; render(true); });
  $(sv).addEventListener("pointercancel", () => { st.drag = null; });
}

/* ---------- controls ---------- */
function setDeg(){
  st.pxi = +$("pxi").value; st.peta = +$("peta").value;
  st.cp = defaultCP(st.pxi, st.peta);           // node count changed, so rebuild
  fitView(); render(true);
}
$("pxi").addEventListener("input", setDeg);
$("peta").addEventListener("input", setDeg);

$("xi").addEventListener("input",  e => { st.xi  = +e.target.value; render(false); });
$("eta").addEventListener("input", e => { st.eta = +e.target.value; render(false); });
$("xi_n").addEventListener("change",  e => { const v = parseFloat(e.target.value); if (Number.isFinite(v)){ st.xi  = clamp(v); render(false);} });
$("eta_n").addEventListener("change", e => { const v = parseFloat(e.target.value); if (Number.isFinite(v)){ st.eta = clamp(v); render(false);} });

for (const id of ["t_weights","t_grid","t_labels"]) $(id).addEventListener("change", () => render(false));
$("b_reset").addEventListener("click", () => { st.cp = defaultCP(st.pxi, st.peta); fitView(); render(true); });
$("b_fit").addEventListener("click",   () => { fitView(); render(false); });

/* ---------- go ---------- */
st.cp = defaultCP(st.pxi, st.peta);
fitView();
render(true);
})();
</script>
```

## Reading the four lines

The block to the right of the table is the same computation written four times.

1. **The sum, symbolically.** One term per node, so the number of terms changes with the
   degree: $n_{en} = (p_\xi+1)(p_\eta+1)$.
2. **Nodal coordinates substituted.** The $\underline{x}_A$ are now numbers, the ones in
   the table. The parametric point has not been used yet.
3. **Basis functions evaluated.** Now $(\xi,\eta)$ is used and each $N_A$ becomes a
   number. This is the only line that changes when you move the dot without changing the
   element.
4. **The mapped point.** Multiply and add.

The term in red has the largest weight. Move the dot to a node and that weight becomes
$1$ while the others become $0$, which is the interpolation property from Class 11.

Below the table is the running value of $\sum_A N_A(\xi,\eta)$, which is $1$ everywhere.
This is the **partition of unity**, and it says a constant is reproduced exactly: if every
$\underline{x}_A$ were the same point, the map would return that point for any
$(\xi,\eta)$. It is the $[0,0]$ case of the reproduction question in Homework 6,
Problem 3.

## The basis functions

This page does not plot the 2D basis functions. The node markers in the parent domain
show $N_A(\xi,\eta)$ at the current point, which is what is needed here. To see the
surfaces themselves, go back to [Class 11](11_Class.qmd).

## Things to try

1. Drag the dot to the corner $(\xi,\eta) = (-1,-1)$. The mapped point is control point
   $0$, and in line 3 every weight is zero except that one.
2. Set $p_\xi = p_\eta = 1$. There are four nodes and the edges are straight: a bilinear
   map cannot curve an edge. The mapped grid lines are still not parallel, so the map is
   not affine.
3. Go back to degree 2 and drag the mid-edge control point $A = 1$, at $(a,b) = (1,0)$,
   away from the edge. The edge bends. This is how a quadratic element follows a curved
   boundary.
4. Keep moving that node past its neighbours until the mapped grid lines cross. The map
   is no longer one-to-one and the element has folded. Nothing in the sum prevents this.
5. Set $p_\xi = 3$, $p_\eta = 1$: cubic in $\xi$, linear in $\eta$, eight nodes. The
   stride $A = a + (p_\xi+1)b$ renumbers the table.
6. Put the dot at $(\xi,\eta) = (0,0)$ and read line 3. At degree 2 in both directions the
   centre node has weight $1$ and the rest have weight $0$; at degree 1 the four corners
   each have weight $0.25$. The centre of the element is a node only when the degree is
   even.

## Next

The map says where a parametric point goes. It does not say how much a small piece of the
parent domain is stretched or rotated on the way, and we need that to write
$\int_{\Omega^e} (\cdot)\,d\Omega$ as an integral over the parent domain that quadrature
can evaluate. Differentiating the sum with respect to $\underline{\xi}$ gives the
deformation gradient and its determinant, the **Jacobian**, in Class 13. Item 4 above is
the case where that determinant changes sign.
